Build is ignored. Good. Working tree only contains the intended changes. `MM src/resolver.h` means staged + unstaged modifications (auto-commit weirdness), but the working tree content is what matters.

Wait, other src files (logger.h, command_lint.cc, command_validate.cc, command_bundle.cc) are not shown as modified because they were auto-committed into HEAD and no further changes. That's fine; the working tree still contains them and they differ from the starting commit fc0dd94. The submit mechanism captures working tree. But hold on: "The working tree at this instant -- committed, modified, and untracked files alike ... captured as the answer." So committed changes count too. Good.

Actually, one concern: submit refuses "when the tree is identical to the starting commit". The starting commit presumably fc0dd94. Our HEAD is effc10e with changes. Not identical. Fine.

But there's a subtle risk: the auto-commit hook might interpret my `submit`? No.

Let me double-check the full diff from fc0dd94 one more time to ensure no accidental changes elsewhere (e.g., clang-format didn't reformat unrelated files). `git diff fc0dd94 --stat`. It should show only the 5 files (4 src + 1 test). Note logger.h etc. are committed in intermediate commits, and git diff fc0dd94 includes committed changes. Let me run.

Then update checklist and submit.
